questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Picking where to study boiled down to a few key things for me: awesome culture, great weather, and a bit of a focus on academics. It was about finding a place that had the right balance of fun and learning.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The school is situated right at the beachfront of carcavelos and has really nice facilities, however the academic level was a bit below what i anticipated and there is alot of group work

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a welcome day and all information was given prior to the exchange by email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not so easy. Use places like uniplaces or inlife to find a room/apartment in Lisbon. Spot-a-Home also works but is a bit more sketchy. Search for a place as soon as you can, I waited too long and ended up with a place that was expensive and  not very nice.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Unless you only go for surfing, it is way more fun to stay in Lisbon than Carcavelos

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: NOVA SBE has a bidding system for courses on master level which can be slightly tricky. Make sure to go to the online orientation about this. Also you are not allowed to take courses that overlap so be aware of this when bidding

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online orientation

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up with all of the courses i bid on, however, I would have like to taken different courses but due to an overlap in scheduling this was not possible

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Attendance is not mandatory on master level. you can check if it part of the grade in a given course in the course catalogue. I spent way to much time planning not having classes on fridays.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: General academic level was lower than at UCPH. I had the courses Machine learning, which was actually a quite elaborate intro to machine learning with some very useful code. Intro to Programming - very easy if you know python and a very small curriculum compared to the 7 ects. Banking - had little to do with economics of banking. Applied corporate finance, and Health economics which was also quite easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Compared to the master courses at UCPH there is a lot of mandatory assignments and group work,  this can be very time demanding. If you want to avoid this check the grading scheme of the course in the course catalouge

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Machine learning, Intro to Programming, Applied Corporate Finance, Banking and Heath Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Machine learning - if you already know some python, Intro to Programming - if you are new to programming

questions.answer: Transportation was only 40 eur a month and with the card you could go to places like Cascai, Sintra and so on

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of activities organised by the student union.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I heard very good thing of the 3 day surfing in the intro program

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Transportation by bus is really easy in portugal if you want to go to Porto, or Faro it only takes 3 hours and cost something like 50 kr with flixbus. you can also get very cheap flights to Madeira or the Azores.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy people are very friendly and there are a lot of other exchange students

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the sunset bars at Nova!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Trains were striking a lot during my stay, which made the transportation from lisbon to carcavelos very difficult

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very easy going culture with a lot of party

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
* If you want to stay in lisbon I would recommend staying near cais do sodre in order for a smooth transport to Campus 
* Remember to book accommodation as soon as possible
* Be aware of the workload associated with groupwork in large groups

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: In order to get the transportation card go to the Metro station at Marques de Pombal here there is a rapid service close to the blue line. Bring a passport photo of yourself, your passport and fill out the form.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends and exploring Lisbon and Portugal

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trains

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
